name: Stare Mesto (Historic Square)
tagline: The pastel heart of Telc, and the whole reason to come
description: The historic core built around namesti Zachariase z Hradce, ringed by Renaissance and Baroque arcaded houses, the chateau and fishponds. This is where nearly all restaurants, cafes and shops sit, and where day-trip tourists concentrate in summer. Staying here means postcard views out your window and everything within a two-minute walk, at the cost of some daytime foot traffic and slightly higher rents than the rest of town.
vibe: Historic, picturesque, touristy by day and calm by evening
bestFor: Short stays, first-time visitors, anyone prioritizing atmosphere over quiet
pros: Walk to everything, including the chateau and fishponds
Stunning architecture right outside your door
Best restaurant and cafe access in town
cons: Busiest with tour groups in summer daytime
Slightly pricier rentals than surrounding areas

name: Podoli
tagline: Quiet residential streets just beyond the ponds
description: A low-key residential district a short walk south of the old town, separated from the square by one of Telc's fishponds. Podoli offers cheaper, more local housing with easy lakeside walking paths and a genuinely residential, non-touristy feel. It suits nomads who want proximity to the historic center without living inside the tourist zone itself, trading a five to ten minute walk for noticeably more peace and quiet.
bestFor: Longer stays, budget-conscious renters, those wanting distance from tourist crowds
pros: Cheaper rents than the old town
Direct access to fishpond walking paths
cons: 10 to 15 minute walk to restaurants and shops
Very little going on locally after dark

name: Stepnice
description: A newer residential area on the edge of town, home to the supermarket, some schools and ordinary Czech family housing. Stepnice is the least scenic part of Telc but the most practical, useful for longer-term stays where daily errands and grocery access matter more than views. It is a ten to fifteen minute walk from the historic square, quiet, functional, and about as far from the tourist experience as Telc gets.
bestFor: Long-term budget stays, families, anyone prioritizing practicality over charm
pros: Closest area to the main supermarket
cons: Farthest walk from the square and chateau

name: Dacice
tagline: A nearby town for day trips, errands, and a change of pace
description: A larger town about 20 minutes from Telc by bus or car, useful as a practical satellite for bigger grocery runs, a wider choice of shops, and a bit more everyday bustle than Telc itself offers. Dacice is not a nomad base in its own right but a handy nearby option for anyone based in Telc who wants occasional variety, additional services, or a slightly bigger-town feel without traveling all the way to Jihlava or Brno.
bestFor: Day trips, errands, a break from Telc's small-town pace
pros: Wider shopping and services than Telc
Less touristy, more everyday Czech life
cons: Lacks Telc's UNESCO architecture and charm
Not a realistic base, more of a supplementary trip
